set.approach: Rescue Rock is a small outcrop just north of US 285 along County Road 60 near Grant. LKP is an easy trad line with a small overhanging roof at the top-out, protected with a standard rack of cams.
set.descent_text: Walk off to the climber's left (east) by descending a short chimney or crack, or rappel from rocks at the top.

review.notes: Route page for the walk-off or rappel and the line; area page for the road position.

set.approach: Start at the Glacier Gorge trailhead and walk toward Loch Vale. At the Andrews Glacier junction, which is easy to miss, keep low in the valley beside the glacial runoff rather than following the trail up toward the glacier; that lower line avoids the worst of the boulders on the way to the Gash. Hike up the Gash, the large boulderfield below the rock, and as you near the spire a long fin of rock comes off the northeast ridge. Climb to the east of that fin and scramble up large ledges to start.
set.descent_text: From the summit, cairns lead down a small gully to the southeast to bolted rappel anchors. A few rappels reach the top of the Gash, with a class 3 downclimb after the last one, and the Gash takes you down to the trail.

review.notes: Route page and Sharkstooth area page both describe the cairned summit-to-rappel descent into the Gash; area page gives the trail junction advice.

set.approach: Hike the Long's Peak trail to the saddle above treeline where it forks, then bear left on the signed branch to Chasm Lake. The prow-shaped formation standing just uphill and south of the lake is the Ship's Prow; it lies right of the long talus slope that climbs toward the Loft. Barnacle Scars begins just right of the Portal: follow the lower pitches of Keel Haul, then branch onto the new line from the belay above them.
set.descent_text: Getting down from the formation can be done by rappelling, by following the ridge west to the far side of Chasm Lake, or by a ramp right of the Great Dihedral, where rappelling is worth considering.

review.notes: Area page for approach and formation descents; route page for the start.

set.approach: Hike the Long's Peak trail to the saddle above treeline where it forks, then bear left on the signed branch to Chasm Lake. The prow-shaped formation standing just uphill and south of the lake is the Ship's Prow; it lies right of the long talus slope that climbs toward the Loft. Raise the Main begins on the opening pitch common to Yard Arms and Keel Haul, up to a good ledge with a fixed piton at the belay; the steep wall above follows.
set.descent_text: Lower from the fixed anchor at the end of the crux pitch, or belay there and continue by a short corner to the cliff top. Getting down from the formation can be done by rappelling, by following the ridge west to the far side of Chasm Lake, or by a ramp right of the Great Dihedral, where rappelling is worth considering.

review.notes: Route page for the lower-off or short top corner; area page for the formation descents.

set.approach: Hike the Long's Peak trail to the saddle above treeline where it forks, then bear left on the signed branch to Chasm Lake. The prow-shaped formation standing just uphill and south of the lake is the Ship's Prow; it lies right of the long talus slope that climbs toward the Loft. Slocum's Spray starts around the corner from Sarchasm: traverse a narrow third-class ledge and belay from a slung block. The route is a long single pitch just left of Etch-a-Sketch.
set.descent_text: Getting down from the formation can be done by rappelling, by following the ridge west to the far side of Chasm Lake, or by a ramp right of the Great Dihedral, where rappelling is worth considering.

review.notes: Area page for approach and formation descents; route page for the start.

set.approach: Hike the Long's Peak trail to the saddle above treeline where it forks, then bear left on the signed branch to Chasm Lake. The prow-shaped formation standing just uphill and south of the lake is the Ship's Prow; it lies right of the long talus slope that climbs toward the Loft. The Plank starts on Bologna Pony, climbs the crack, and traverses right at a small roof to an anchor; the other two pitches go up the bolted face above.
set.descent_text: The route can be descended on a single long rope. Getting down from the formation can be done by rappelling, by following the ridge west to the far side of Chasm Lake, or by a ramp right of the Great Dihedral, where rappelling is worth considering.

review.notes: Route page for the start and single-rope descent; area page for approach and formation descents.

set.approach: Park near Sleeping Elephant Campground in the Poudre Canyon, cross the river, avoid the private property, and walk up the talus to the base of the wall. There are no trails, and the crossing is part of the route's character. The route climbs the northeast face and begins with a short bolted approach pitch to the first belay anchors.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route from its bolted belay stations, or walk off to the climber's left or right. A left walk-off follows a drainage toward the talus, or you can hike over the summit and descend the next drainage to the south. The approach talus is awkward going down.

review.notes: Route page for start and both descents; area page for parking and river crossing.

set.approach: This north-facing buttress in the Gore Range can be reached two ways. The simpler way starts at the Rock Creek trailhead, follows the Freya Tower approach, and then drops southeast into the valley below to the buttress. The other follows the Gore Range Trail south to the bridge over South Rock Creek, then bushwhacks west up the creek past meadows and small outcrops to the base. The route starts at a small rock pillar at the foot of the climb, directly beneath the obvious offwidth on the second pitch.

review.notes: Area page for both approaches; route page for the start. No descent stated.

set.approach: Park in the pullout along Mount Blue Sky Road and go down the gully, then follow the Abyss Lake trail south-southwest toward the wall's base. Looking northwest from the stretch between Helms Lake and Lake Fork, the wall is hard to miss; no maintained path leaves the trail for the base, so tread lightly on the tundra. The route begins in the loose chimney of Right of Passage, then breaks left onto the face before the chimney ends, passing left of the crux roof.
set.descent_text: Walk off to climber's right via obvious grassy ledges, with perhaps a fourth-class move or two.

review.notes: Route page for the approach, start and walk-off; area page for the Abyss Lake trail approach and wall position.

set.approach: Trails from the Glacier Gorge trailhead lead to Black Lake. At Stoneman Pass, go east along the divide's south side toward Chiefshead to the conspicuous tower, walk beyond it, and descend northward. Downclimb north to the tower's east side, then use third- and fourth-class ground to swing round to the northeast side and enter a gully. Belay anywhere; climbing to near the summit makes the belay simpler.

review.notes: Route page for the tower approach; area page for the Black Lake access. No descent stated.

set.approach: The approach goes up Elk Creek to the trail into the Vestal drainage and continues east past a lake, over a pass between two high points. There is good camping with views of the north faces near the tarns, and an obscure trail at the tarn level contours toward the southeast ridge. The route gains the broad northeast ridge and follows it: easier ground first, then a narrowing ridge to the base of a tower that holds the crux.

review.notes: Area page for the Elk Creek approach; route page for the line. No descent stated.

set.approach: Park at the pulloff by the sheep sign just past the eighteenth highway marker and follow the Hero Traverse east to the Corinthian Column. Turn left there and head down toward the Bottomless Pit, hugging skier's left. At the base of the ridge is a short buttress with several splitter cracks for the first pitch. The ridge runs up out of the pit and joins the Hero Traverse, where you can bail to the right or continue.

review.notes: Route page for the approach and the ridge; area page is a placeholder. No descent stated.

set.approach: This is the mountaineer's route up T3 in the Block Tops. Reach the T3 and T4 saddle by way of T4, rappelling off the west end of T4's summit ridge, then cross the rotten catwalk in the saddle and scramble up solid blocks to a platform below the east face. The route is at the northeast corner: from the base of the wall make a descending traverse north on bad orange rock until you can escape right toward the lower of two big tan blocks.
set.descent_text: Heading on to T2 means walking to the summit ridge's west end and rappelling from boulders to the scree. Going back to the T3-T4 saddle instead uses a rappel from the bolted anchor high on the east face.

review.notes: Route page for the access and both rappels; T3 area page for the saddle approach.

set.approach: Leave the car at Summit Lake and use the climbers' trail on Spaulding, the same start as for the Black Wall. Cross the top of the Black Wall and go a little farther until a ramp-and-ledge system shows on your right; drop packs at the head of it and downclimb the ramp to the foot of the buttresses. The route begins on a broken pillar beside Noth'N But a Good Time (to its right), then follows a prominent right-leaning ramp system toward the middle meadow of the wall.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for the start. No descent stated.

set.approach: Tava Buttress is a sunny east-facing buttress on the Pikes Peak highway. From Devil's Playground, hike due east and slightly uphill to the ridge, then head through the saddle that sits below to the southeast and down the loose grus at class 2, aiming right and south below the wall to the base. The approach crosses a barrier along the summit trail, so stay on rock to reduce impact. The upper start is an eye-catching right-facing corner holding a wide crack, and a second, meandering start begins somewhat lower.
set.descent_text: The way out climbs rather than descends: work right along a ledge and gully, taking the ledge's easy scrambling to dodge the worst of the gully. It ends on a patch of tundra and talus, from which you walk to the trail and road and follow the road back to the pullout.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page for the starts and the descent.

set.approach: Take the approach to the Rolling Stones Wall, then keep going east along the fence line to the escarpment edge and south to the slot that separates the main cliff from The Citadel. Bachelor Pizza climbs the north face of The Citadel from the base of the approach rappel, which goes down the slot from a bolted anchor with chains. It works as a handy way up to the tower's top, from where the south-face routes are rappelled.

review.notes: Area page for the approach and slot rappel; route page for the purpose of the line. No descent stated.

set.approach: Take the approach to the Rolling Stones Wall, then keep going east along the fence line to the escarpment edge and south to the slot that separates the main cliff from The Citadel. This one-pitch line goes up the left-facing corner to the right of Jimmy Bucket, then a hand crack on the face farther right, and ends at the two-bolt anchor that Texas Wheelchair's third pitch shares.

review.notes: Area page and sibling approach text as named on the route; route page for the line. No descent stated.

set.approach: Take the Rolling Stones Wall approach and go down the gully on its north side to a bolted slab that faces south at a low angle. A second way in is to climb Bachelor Pizza, on The Citadel's north face, and rappel that line. The first pitch is a bolted slab to an anchor on a large ledge, and the line continues up a pillar beside a bolted dihedral.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route itself, or use the chains at the top to make one rappel down the tower's north face.

review.notes: Route page for the approach and for both descent options.

set.approach: Approach as for Tempest, by way of the Rolling Stones Wall and the gully north of it. This variation shares the lower pitches of Tempest and then diverges right from the big grassy ledge, avoiding the steep roof and staying on easier ground.
set.descent_text: Descend as for Tempest: rappel the route, or take the chains at the top for a rappel down the tower's north face.

review.notes: Route page names Tempest's descent as its own; Tempest page lists both options.

set.approach: Take the approach to the Rolling Stones Wall, then keep going east along the fence line to the escarpment edge and south to the slot that separates the main cliff from The Citadel. This line is on the south face: drop down the gully north of the Rolling Stones Wall to a ledge beneath that wall. It climbs moderate runout ground on small gear, then steep cracks and a corner, and finishes in a blocky chimney.

review.notes: Area page and route page for approach. No descent stated.

set.approach: In the town of Crestone drive east on East Galena Avenue to its end at the trailhead and hike the Willow Lake trail up to the Willow Lake campground. The route climbs the prominent face just south of the campground, starting on the left side of the talus below the cliff.
set.descent_text: Once the climbing turns to second class, bear northwest onto easier slopes that run down toward the lake's north shore. Following the ridge to Challenger Point and then the Mountaineer's trail back to the campground is the better option.

review.notes: Route page for approach, start and descent.

set.approach: The route can be reached from the Spanish Creek, Willow Lakes or South Colony Lakes trailheads. The Spanish Creek approach crosses private monastery land and needs a permit arranged ahead. The Prow is the fin on the southwest ridge of Kit Carson Mountain, of Crestone conglomerate. Scramble third class to the base of the fin, and the first move up a bulge begins the route.
set.descent_text: Head east a long way, going over another peak, to the wide valley in the saddle separating Kit Carson from Ellingwood, which allows a return to camp. Cutting back early leads onto steep slabs.

review.notes: Route page for approach options, start and descent.

set.approach: Follow any Sneffels north face approach, then continue southwest up the drainage to the cluster of pinnacles at its head. To avoid talus, scramble up a rock buttress on the right (west) to an orange ledge below the east side of Number One, that gives access to the pinnacles' north side and The Hand. The col north of The Hand can be gained from Blaine Basin; the route starts just right of the north arete.
set.descent_text: Reverse the route, or rappel from a slung block into the grassy gully northwest of the south summit, then a second rappel drops into the south gully that runs between The Hand and The Penguin. The broad gully separating those two pinnacles also serves as a way down.

review.notes: Route page for start and descents; The Hand area page for approach.

set.approach: Follow any Sneffels north face approach, continue southwest up the drainage to the pinnacles at its head, and reach their north side by scrambling a rock buttress to the right and an orange ledge. Climb the talus gully to the notch dividing The Hand from The Penguin, then make an easy third-class scramble up and right to the clear east crack.
set.descent_text: Either rappel the crack, or walk around to the west side and downclimb loose fourth-class ground into the Penguin-Thumb saddle.

review.notes: Route page for the start and both descents; Penguin area page for the approach.

set.approach: This is a far-off north-facing buttress in the valley south of the Walk of Life Spire. Begin at the pond and meadow under the spire's scree field and follow the side valley that branches south, right to the foot of the Stargate. The route climbs the weakness just left of the centre of the buttress.
set.descent_text: Go down the avalanche chute on the buttress's east side, which faces north, to reach the valley. The chute is avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page and area page agree on the east chute descent; area page for approach.

set.approach: Follow any Sneffels north face approach, continue southwest up the drainage to the pinnacles, and reach their north side via a rock buttress and an orange ledge. The sharp saddle between The Penguin and The Thumb is gained through the north talus gully or from The Penguin itself; then work west up the slopes until the angle kicks up. The route follows a shallow depression on the southeast face.
set.descent_text: Sling or build an anchor in the plentiful cracks and rappel back down to the approach slopes.

review.notes: Route page for the saddle approach and rappel; Thumb area page for the approach.

set.approach: Leave the car at the lot by the sixteenth highway marker and walk east to the ridge's high point. Locate the gash in the south side and The Blade. Hiking down the Dinosaur Couloir and scrambling up to the base is possible, but rappelling in has less effect on the terrain and the sheep; the anchors are set in a groove behind the top-out, with another farther down and to skier's right, and the gully below leads around to the base. The route starts on the left side of the formation, aiming for a laser-cut fist crack.

review.notes: Route page and The Wall area page for approach; no descent stated after the top-out.

set.approach: Leave the car at the lot by the sixteenth highway marker and walk east up to the ridge. Two ways lead in. One uses the Katana Ridge rappels, then crosses broken ledges beyond its base to the grassy ledges below the first pitch. The other rappels in from this route's top, a short way over to the skier's right from Katana Ridge's summit, at a roomy ledge split by a wide crack in a dihedral. The route is on the left of The Wall, following a thin dihedral system into the conspicuous wide crack.

review.notes: Route page for both approaches; The Wall area page for the parking and ridge. No descent stated beyond a short rappel to the belay ledge.
